answer: In an AI-agent marketplace for surveys of mesa terrain, delta channels, and shale beds, each bidding identity must lock a bond for 30 days, and its total outstanding work cannot exceed that bond. Payment waits for delivery checks; provable nondelivery forfeits the bond. Creating fake identities therefore adds no unbacked capacity: to win more work at once, an attacker must lock proportionally more capital and risk losing it on every failed contract.
